system_overview: This specification models the Yo-Yo leader election algorithm for connected undirected graphs without pruning, as introduced by Nicola Santoro. The algorithm elects the node with the smallest identity as leader by orienting edges and iteratively eliminating candidate source nodes through alternating downward and upward message-passing phases. Without pruning, the algorithm stabilizes but does not terminate, as no node can detect that stabilization has occurred.
actors_and_components: The participants are nodes in a connected undirected graph, each identified by a unique integer. Nodes communicate by sending messages to neighbors along directed edges. Nodes are classified dynamically as sources (only outgoing edges), sinks (only incoming edges), or internal nodes (both incoming and outgoing edges). Sources are candidates for leadership.
state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state per node: (1) the current phase of the node (downward or upward), (2) the set of incoming neighbors (nodes from which edges point toward this node), (3) the set of outgoing neighbors (nodes toward which edges point away from this node), and (4) a mailbox containing pending messages. Messages are of two types: downward-phase messages carrying a sender identifier and a value (the minimum identity seen), and upward-phase messages carrying a sender identifier and a yes-or-no reply.
initial_state: All nodes start in the downward phase. Edges are oriented from smaller to larger node identity: each node's incoming neighbors are those neighbors with smaller identities, and outgoing neighbors are those with larger identities. All mailboxes are empty. This initial orientation ensures that the node with the globally smallest identity is a source.
actions: The algorithm proceeds in rounds of two phases. In the downward phase: source nodes broadcast their own identity to all outgoing neighbors and switch to the upward phase. Non-source nodes wait until they have received a downward message from every incoming neighbor, then forward the minimum received value to all outgoing neighbors and switch to the upward phase. In the upward phase: sink nodes (which have no outgoing edges and thus receive no upward replies) examine the downward messages received, reply 'yes' to all incoming neighbors that sent the minimum value and 'no' to all others, then switch to the downward phase. Internal nodes wait until they have received an upward reply from every outgoing neighbor. If any reply is 'no', they send 'no' to all incoming neighbors. Otherwise, they send 'yes' to incoming neighbors that sent the smallest value during the downward phase and 'no' to all others. Source nodes wait for upward replies from all outgoing neighbors; neighbors that sent 'no' become incoming neighbors (edge reversal). After the upward phase, edges along which 'no' was sent reverse their direction, potentially changing node classifications.
safety_properties: A neighbor consistency invariant holds: a node has another as an outgoing neighbor if and only if the other has the first as an incoming neighbor, except when an edge is being reversed (indicated by a pending 'no' message in one of their mailboxes). No new source nodes are created during execution: if a node becomes a source, it was already a source. Type correctness ensures all variables remain in their expected domains.
liveness_properties: The system eventually stabilizes to a state where there is exactly one source node (the one with the smallest identity), all downward messages carry that node's identity, and all upward messages say 'yes'. However, the algorithm does not terminate because no node can detect this stabilization.
model_bounds: The graph topology (nodes and edges) is provided as constants. The model-checking configuration uses a five-node graph with specific edges.
additional_assumptions: The specification assumes the graph is connected and undirected with no self-loops, and all node identities are distinct integers. Weak fairness is assumed on the next-state action. The algorithm uses asynchronous message passing where each node can take a step independently when its preconditions are met.
